result.scope:
Exercise notification navigation through real desktop processes and private IPC.

This tests existing-window and cold-start routing with actual daemon state and
rendered controls. It does not simulate or claim a Notification Center click.
Native sender authorization and physical notification clicks are separate trials.

installation_assertions: Copied application files, modes and hashes equal the inspected retained signed payload; codesign --verify --deep --strict passes.
Legacy absolute hook/MCP paths and all three executable roles work after activation and rollback.
The MCP process executes the selected immutable version, checked with ps; the older pre-capability symlink alias is canonicalized, while copied executables remain distinct paths.
The actual older build bootstraps its historical launcher using its own installer. The new installer retains a compatible signed copy when rolling back to that older payload.
Existing fixture daemon stays responsive; cleanup retains live pins and compatible launcher payload; uninstall preserves daemon state.
navigation_assertions: Driver starts through a separately installed intact application copy under a private prefix.
24 existing-window and two cold-start steps passed in 9.626 seconds; all eight destination/draft checks passed.
Retained answer-draft and cold-route screenshots were visually inspected.
No surviving fixture children; binary hashes unchanged.

The older package is a separate clean build of b605f8e with the same state schema, not relabelled metadata. The only subsequent executable-trial driver change resolves historical symlink aliases in ps output; production Rust source is unchanged.
